title: Reward-rate reset on every non-zero pull / top-up back-loads emissions and rounds user accruals down on each reset
description:
Whenever `_syncBudget` sees non-zero inflow, or `topUp` runs, or `setWindowDuration` runs, the code sets `windowEnd = block.timestamp + windowDuration` AND recomputes `rewardRate = rewardBudget / windowDuration`. Aside from the rate-dust issue covered in CS-02, this has a second rounding consequence: the new rate is derived from the NEW `rewardBudget`, which still includes the untruncated residual from the OLD schedule. On each reset the residual is re-divided by the full windowDuration, which truncates again. Over N resets, the truncation compounds, and users' total claimable emissions are strictly less than the sum of inflows.

Separately, the back-loading semantics mean that if resets happen frequently (e.g., dispatcher pulls on every user action, which is the exact design), the effective emission schedule is asymptotically slower than `budget/windowDuration` — each new inflow gets its own fresh 540-day window instead of being amortized over the remaining window. This is the stated spec behavior, but combined with the floor-division re-truncation it favors the protocol at every step; the user-side rounding direction is consistent but the magnitude is larger than the 1-wei-per-accrual assumed in the `_safePay` comment.
impact: Cumulative under-distribution of rewards to stakers across many pull/topUp cycles. The protocol retains the dust — consistent with the user's stated 'round in favor of protocol' requirement — but the design doesn't appear to account for the compounded magnitude, which can become large (up to `N * windowDuration` wei) over the life of the pool.
proof: Sequence: start with `rewardBudget = 0`. Do N pulls, each bringing in `X` wei of phUSD. After pull 1: `rewardRate = X/D`, residual = `X mod D`. Before any elapsed time, pull 2 brings `X`; new budget = `X + X = 2X - 0` (no accrual yet). `rewardRate = 2X/D`, residual = `2X mod D`. Each fresh reset re-truncates the residual. If consumers interleave accrual and pulls rapidly enough that `elapsed * rewardRate` is small, the residual floor stays nearly constant and leaks dust each cycle.
recommendation: Amortize inflow into the REMAINING window rather than resetting to a full new window. Compute `remaining = windowEnd > now ? windowEnd - now : windowDuration; rewardRate = (rewardBudget) / remaining` (still floor, still protocol-favoring, but re-truncation is minimized since the denominator shrinks each reset). Alternatively, track accrual with `rewardBudget * elapsed / windowDuration` directly and avoid the intermediate `rewardRate` variable entirely. Add a test that asserts sum-of-claimed-rewards <= sum-of-inflows (already true) AND sum-of-claimed-rewards >= sum-of-inflows - O(windowDuration) (likely not true today).
